description: The formulas of the propagation of uncertainty (Wikipedia: Propagation_of_uncertainty): the variance of a function of uncertain inputs for a scaled quantity, a sum, a difference, a linear combination, a product and a quotient, each in the variance form that the calculation engine can reproduce, plus the standard deviation forms of the example table (power, logarithm, exponential, trigonometric function, general power and root) and the first order formula as documentation. The sample inputs x = 3 and y = 2 with the standard deviations 0.3 and 0.4, the correlation 0.2 and the coefficients a = 2 and b = 5 are assumed to make every variance formula reproducible by a calc-validation.

words.name: propagation
words.description: the spreading of an effect from its source, e.g. of the uncertainty of the inputs to the result of a calculation

words.name: uncertainty
words.description: epistemic situations involving imperfect or unknown information, in measurements the range in which the true value is expected

words.name: statistics
words.description: Statistics is the discipline that concerns the collection, organization, analysis, interpretation, and presentation of data.

words.name: variance
words.description: In probability theory and statistics, variance is the expectation of the squared deviation of a random variable from its mean.

words.name: covariance
words.description: In probability theory and statistics, covariance is a measure of the joint variability of two random variables.

words.name: correlation
words.description: In statistics, correlation or dependence is any statistical relationship, whether causal or not, between two random variables.

words.name: deviation
words.description: In mathematics and statistics, deviation is a measure of difference between the observed value of a variable and some other value, often that variable's mean.

words.name: standard
words.description: describes the conventional reference form, e.g. standard deviation

words.name: sigma
words.description: the symbol of the standard deviation of a quantity

words.name: linear
words.description: relating to a straight line or to a function of the first degree

words.name: combination
words.description: an expression built from a set of terms, e.g. by adding each term multiplied by a coefficient

words.name: scaling
words.description: the multiplication of a quantity by a constant factor

words.name: sum
words.description: the result of adding two or more numbers

words.name: quotient
words.description: the result of dividing one number by another

words.name: power
words.description: the result of raising a number to an exponent

words.name: exponential
words.description: a function in which the variable is the exponent

words.name: logarithm
words.description: the inverse function of exponentiation, the exponent to which a base must be raised to produce a number

words.name: Goodman
words.description: American statistician after whom the exact variance of a product of two independent random variables is named

triples.description: the effect of the uncertainties of the inputs on the uncertainty of a function of these inputs

triples.name: linear combination
triples.description: an expression built from a set of terms by multiplying each term by a coefficient and adding the results

triples.name: correlation coefficient
triples.description: a numerical measure of the linear correlation between two random variables, between -1 and 1
the standard deviation of the input x
the standard deviation of the input y
the standard deviation of the result f
the variance of the input x, the square of its standard deviation
the variance of the input y, the square of its standard deviation
the variance of the result f, the square of its standard deviation
the covariance of the inputs x and y, zero if the inputs are independent

formulas.name: variance from the standard deviation
formulas.description: the variance of a quantity is the square of its standard deviation, so a measurement uncertainty given as sigma can be used in the variance based propagation formulas
formulas.expression: "variance of x" = "sigma of x" * "sigma of x"

formulas.name: covariance from the correlation
formulas.description: the covariance of two inputs from their correlation coefficient and their standard deviations; the covariance is zero for independent inputs and then drops out of the propagation formulas
formulas.expression: "covariance of x and y" = "correlation coefficient" * "sigma of x" * "sigma of y"
formulas.latex: \text{covariance of x and y} = \text{correlation coefficient} \cdot \text{sigma of x} \cdot \text{sigma of y}

formulas.name: propagation for a scaled quantity
formulas.description: the uncertainty of a result that is an input multiplied by a constant, f = a x: the variance is scaled by the square of the constant, so the standard deviation is scaled by the constant itself
formulas.expression: "variance of f" = "a" * "a" * "variance of x"

formulas.name: propagation for a sum
formulas.description: the uncertainty of a result that is the sum of two uncertain inputs, f = x + y: the variances add up, plus twice the covariance if the inputs are correlated; for independent inputs the standard deviations add in quadrature
formulas.expression: "variance of f" = "variance of x" + "variance of y" + 2 * "covariance of x and y"
formulas.latex: \text{variance of f} = \text{variance of x} + \text{variance of y} + 2 \cdot \text{covariance of x and y}

formulas.name: propagation for a difference
formulas.description: the uncertainty of a result that is the difference of two uncertain inputs, f = x - y: the variances add up like for a sum, but a positive correlation reduces the uncertainty, because a common error cancels in the difference
formulas.expression: "variance of f" = "variance of x" + "variance of y" - 2 * "covariance of x and y"
formulas.latex: \text{variance of f} = \text{variance of x} + \text{variance of y} - 2 \cdot \text{covariance of x and y}

formulas.name: propagation for a linear combination
formulas.description: the uncertainty of a result that is a weighted sum of two uncertain inputs, f = a x + b y: each variance is scaled by the square of its weight and the covariance term by the product of the weights
formulas.expression: "variance of f" = "a" * "a" * "variance of x" + "b" * "b" * "variance of y" + 2 * "a" * "b" * "covariance of x and y"
formulas.latex: \text{variance of f} = \text{a}^2 \cdot \text{variance of x} + \text{b}^2 \cdot \text{variance of y} + 2 \cdot \text{a} \cdot \text{b} \cdot \text{covariance of x and y}

formulas.name: propagation for a linear difference
formulas.description: the uncertainty of a result that is a weighted difference of two uncertain inputs, f = a x - b y: like the linear combination, but the covariance term is subtracted
formulas.expression: "variance of f" = "a" * "a" * "variance of x" + "b" * "b" * "variance of y" - 2 * "a" * "b" * "covariance of x and y"
formulas.latex: \text{variance of f} = \text{a}^2 \cdot \text{variance of x} + \text{b}^2 \cdot \text{variance of y} - 2 \cdot \text{a} \cdot \text{b} \cdot \text{covariance of x and y}

formulas.name: propagation for a product
formulas.description: f = x y, first order approximation
formulas.expression: "variance of f" = "x" * "y" * "x" * "y" * ( "variance of x" / ( "x" * "x" ) + "variance of y" / ( "y" * "y" ) + 2 * "covariance of x and y" / ( "x" * "y" ) )
formulas.latex: \text{variance of f} \approx \left( \text{x} \cdot \text{y} \right)^2 \left[ \frac{\text{variance of x}}{\text{x}^2} + \frac{\text{variance of y}}{\text{y}^2} + 2 \cdot \frac{\text{covariance of x and y}}{\text{x} \cdot \text{y}} \right]

formulas.name: propagation for a quotient
formulas.description: f = x / y, first order approximation
formulas.expression: "variance of f" = ( "x" / "y" ) * ( "x" / "y" ) * ( "variance of x" / ( "x" * "x" ) + "variance of y" / ( "y" * "y" ) - 2 * "covariance of x and y" / ( "x" * "y" ) )
formulas.latex: \text{variance of f} \approx \left( \frac{\text{x}}{\text{y}} \right)^2 \left[ \frac{\text{variance of x}}{\text{x}^2} + \frac{\text{variance of y}}{\text{y}^2} - 2 \cdot \frac{\text{covariance of x and y}}{\text{x} \cdot \text{y}} \right]

formulas.name: exact variance of a product
formulas.description: f = x y for independent inputs, exact instead of the first order approximation (Goodman)
formulas.expression: "variance of f" = "x" * "x" * "variance of y" + "y" * "y" * "variance of x" + "variance of x" * "variance of y"
formulas.latex: \text{variance of f} = \text{x}^2 \cdot \text{variance of y} + \text{y}^2 \cdot \text{variance of x} + \text{variance of x} \cdot \text{variance of y}

formulas.name: standard deviation of the result
formulas.description: the standard deviation of a result is the square root of its variance, the last step after a variance based propagation to get the uncertainty in the unit of the result
formulas.expression: "sigma of f" = sqrt("variance of f")

formulas.name: propagation for a ratio to the sum
formulas.description: the uncertainty of a share, f = x / (x + y), e.g. the share of one part in the total of two parts; the same input appears in the numerator and the denominator, so the formula differs from the plain quotient
formulas.expression: "sigma of f" = abs("f" / ("x" + "y")) * sqrt("y"^2 / "x"^2 * "variance of x" + "variance of y" - 2 * "y" / "x" * "covariance of x and y")
formulas.latex: \text{sigma of f} \approx \left| \frac{\text{f}}{\text{x} + \text{y}} \right| \sqrt{\frac{\text{y}^2}{\text{x}^2} \cdot \text{variance of x} + \text{variance of y} - 2 \cdot \frac{\text{y}}{\text{x}} \cdot \text{covariance of x and y}}

formulas.name: propagation for a power
formulas.description: the uncertainty of a result that is a power of one uncertain input, f = a x^b: the relative uncertainty of the result is the relative uncertainty of the input multiplied by the absolute value of the exponent, e.g. the area of a square measured with a side length uncertainty of 1% has an uncertainty of 2%; a first order approximation that assumes a small input uncertainty
formulas.expression: "sigma of f" = abs("f" * "b" * "sigma of x" / "x")

formulas.name: propagation for a natural logarithm
formulas.description: the uncertainty of a natural logarithm of an uncertain input, f = a ln(b x): the absolute uncertainty of the result is the relative uncertainty of the input times the factor a, independent of b
formulas.expression: "sigma of f" = abs("a" * "sigma of x" / "x")

formulas.name: propagation for a decimal logarithm
formulas.description: the uncertainty of a decimal logarithm of an uncertain input, f = a log10(b x): like the natural logarithm, but the relative uncertainty of the input is divided by ln(10), e.g. for a pH value
formulas.expression: "sigma of f" = abs("a" * "sigma of x" / ("x" * ln(10)))

formulas.name: propagation for an exponential
formulas.description: the uncertainty of an exponential of an uncertain input, f = a e^(b x): the relative uncertainty of the result is the absolute uncertainty of the input times the exponent factor b, e.g. for a growth or decay over an uncertain time
formulas.expression: "sigma of f" = abs("f" * "b" * "sigma of x")

formulas.name: propagation for a general exponential
formulas.description: the uncertainty of an exponential with a general base, f = a^(b x): like the natural exponential, but the exponent factor is multiplied by the natural logarithm of the base
formulas.expression: "sigma of f" = abs("f" * "b" * ln("a") * "sigma of x")

formulas.name: propagation for a sine
formulas.description: the uncertainty of a sine of an uncertain input, f = a sin(b x): the uncertainty of the input is scaled by the slope of the sine, which is the cosine at the same point, so it is largest near the zero crossings and vanishes at the peaks
formulas.expression: "sigma of f" = abs("a" * "b" * cos("b" * "x") * "sigma of x")

formulas.name: propagation for a cosine
formulas.description: the uncertainty of a cosine of an uncertain input, f = a cos(b x): the uncertainty of the input is scaled by the slope of the cosine, which is the sine at the same point
formulas.expression: "sigma of f" = abs("a" * "b" * sin("b" * "x") * "sigma of x")

formulas.name: propagation for a tangent
formulas.description: the uncertainty of a tangent of an uncertain input, f = a tan(b x): the uncertainty of the input is scaled by the slope of the tangent, the squared secant, which grows without limit near 90 degrees
formulas.expression: "sigma of f" = abs("a" * "b" * sec("b" * "x")^2 * "sigma of x")

formulas.name: propagation for a general power
formulas.description: the uncertainty of a power where both the base and the exponent are uncertain, f = x^y: the relative uncertainty combines the relative uncertainty of the base scaled by the exponent with the uncertainty of the exponent scaled by the logarithm of the base
formulas.expression: "sigma of f" = abs("f") * sqrt(("y" * "sigma of x" / "x")^2 + (ln("x") * "sigma of y")^2 + 2 * "y" * ln("x") * "covariance of x and y" / "x")
formulas.latex: \text{sigma of f} \approx \left| \text{f} \right| \sqrt{\left( \frac{\text{y} \cdot \text{sigma of x}}{\text{x}} \right)^2 + \left( \ln(\text{x}) \cdot \text{sigma of y} \right)^2 + 2 \cdot \frac{\text{y} \cdot \ln(\text{x}) \cdot \text{covariance of x and y}}{\text{x}}}

formulas.name: propagation for a root of a sum of squares
formulas.description: f = sqrt(a x^2 + b y^2), for a difference of the squares the sign of the covariance term flips
formulas.expression: "sigma of f" = sqrt(("x" / "f")^2 * "a"^2 * "variance of x" + ("y" / "f")^2 * "b"^2 * "variance of y" + 2 * "a" * "b" * "x" * "y" * "covariance of x and y" / "f"^2)
formulas.latex: \text{sigma of f} \approx \sqrt{\left( \frac{\text{x}}{\text{f}} \right)^2 \text{a}^2 \cdot \text{variance of x} + \left( \frac{\text{y}}{\text{f}} \right)^2 \text{b}^2 \cdot \text{variance of y} + 2 \cdot \text{a} \cdot \text{b} \cdot \frac{\text{x} \cdot \text{y} \cdot \text{covariance of x and y}}{\text{f}^2}}

formulas.name: propagation to the first order
formulas.description: the variance of any function f of the independent inputs x_i to the first order of the Taylor expansion
formulas.expression: "variance of f" = sum((d"f"/d"x"_"i")^2 * "variance of x"_"i", "i"=1.."n")

formulas.name: standard error of the mean
formulas.description: the standard deviation of the mean of n independent measurements with the standard deviation sigma
formulas.expression: "sigma of f" = "sigma" / sqrt("n")
